evidence.intree_statement: Class Category@{o h p | h <= p} : Type@{max(o+1,h+1,p+1)} := { obj : Type@{o}; ... } — every category lives at a universe strictly above its objects, giving a typed size hierarchy in place of set/class strata
"The name itself has largely fallen out of general use (nLab, 'metacategory'); the size distinctions it once marked are, in this library, carried instead by universe polymorphism."

"a category of all categories invites a Russell-style paradox, classically avoided by the small/large distinction or by Grothendieck universes. Rather than adopt either device axiomatically, this library has a [Cat] at every universe level, each strictly above its own objects"

statement_record.book: Relative to the universe U, a class is any subset of U; small sets (elements of U) are classes; classes not in U (e.g. U itself) are proper classes; small sets and classes together satisfy the Godel-Bernays axioms.
statement_record.intree: No term 'class'/'proper class' exists. The two-level small/class stratification is played by Coq's universe hierarchy, used relatively: Category@{o h p} : Type@{max(o+1,h+1,p+1)} with obj : Type@{o}, and the library headers state explicitly that size distinctions are carried by universe polymorphism.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the ROLE of classes (a size layer above the small sets, usable as the object collection of a large category) is fully served by universe levels and is enforced by the elaborator, but there is no reified definition of class/proper class, no membership relation, and no Godel-Bernays axiom pack — the library formalizes no membership-based set theory.

gap: No membership-based vocabulary: 'class = subset of U', 'proper class = class not in U', and the GB-axioms claim have no in-tree counterparts. Size stratification exists only as Coq's (relative) universe-level discipline, pervasively used but never reified as a predicate or definition.

"The definitions below quantify over [forall (D : Category)] without an explicit smallness hypothesis; the size discipline is instead carried implicitly by the library's universe polymorphism."

evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Sets@{o so} : Category@{so o o} := {| obj := SetoidObject@{o o}; ... |} — the category of ALL setoids at any chosen object universe o; instantiating o at the class level yields the category of class-sized sets, and the typing Category@{so o o} places it strictly above its objects

Definition Setoid_Lift@{o so} (X : SetoidObject@{o o}) : SetoidObject@{so so} — re-types a small setoid one universe up; the file works in Sets@{so sso}, the class-level instantiation, alongside Sets@{o so}

"[PropSetoid] the truth-value setoid: carrier Type@{o} under iffT, a SetoidObject@{so so} (o < so) — one universe up." — a genuinely class-sized object of the higher Sets, used in cross-universe theorems

statement_record.book: Cls is the category whose objects are all classes and whose arrows are all functions between classes; its collection of objects (the power set of U) is not itself a class, so Cls is not given by classes.
statement_record.intree: Sets@{o so} : Category@{so o o} is defined once, universe-polymorphically; instantiated with o at the class level it IS the category of all class-sized sets (setoids) and their maps, and Instance/Sets/Classifier.v actually works in that higher instantiation Sets@{so sso}, with Setoid_Lift and PropSetoid living one universe up. That Cls itself outgrows classes is enforced by the typing (the category lives at universe so strictly above its objects at o).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, up to the library's two standing presentations: sets are rendered as setoids (declared faithful) and the small-set/class stratification is rendered as consecutive universe levels; the book's observation that Cls is not class-given is carried by the universe checker (Category lives strictly above its objects) rather than stated as a cardinality theorem.

evidence.intree_statement: "The first-order theory of categories, and its computable models" — the arrows-only first-order axiomatization on undefined terms, with the machine-checked witness [FromArrows] rebuilding a [Category] from the three axioms; the essay cites Lawvere's elementary programme (ETCS 1964, Category of Categories 1966)

Class ElementaryTopos (C : Category) := { topos_terminal : @Terminal C; topos_cartesian : @Cartesian C; topos_pullbacks : @HasPullbacks C; topos_closed : @Closed C topos_cartesian; topos_classifier : @SubobjectClassifier C topos_terminal } — the elementary (first-order, membership-free) axioms the remark points to

"Reading types and functions as a category enacts the structural stance that Lawvere took when he axiomatized the category of sets directly — objects and composites first, membership a derived notion (... the origin of ETCS). On that view a set is whatever composes, and [Coq] is the stance implemented over the universe Type, machine-checked rather than postulated."

"Lawvere proposed to make the self-application foundational: the category of categories itself, axiomatized in first-order terms, would replace membership-based set theory ... this library has a [Cat] at every universe level, each strictly above its own objects"

statement_record.book: One universe handles the category of all small sets/groups but yields no category of ALL sets; Grothendieck's axiom (every set belongs to some universe) gives one category per universe but still no category of all groups; this motivates set-free first-order axiomatizations — category axioms on undefined terms, and elementary axioms for the category of sets (elementary topos, Mac Lane–Moerdijk).
statement_record.intree: Both first-order alternatives the remark advertises are formalized: the axioms-on-undefined-terms route as Theory/Metacategory.v (arrows-only first-order theory with FromArrows) and the elementary-axioms-for-Set route as Structure/Topos.v's ElementaryTopos (with the computable witness FinSet_Topos, Instance/FinSet/Topos.v:38). The no-category-of-all-X limitation is enforced by universe typing rather than asserted (Instance/Cat.v size note).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker on the set-theoretic half: the one-universe vs Grothendieck-hierarchy comparison is embodied in Coq's metatheory (a cumulative hierarchy with a polymorphic Cat/Sets at every level — functionally Grothendieck's 'every set is in some universe') and discussed in headers, but no membership-based universe or its axioms is formalized; intree-stronger on the axiomatic half: the elementary-topos axioms are not merely cited but defined and inhabited (FinSet_Topos), and the first-order category axioms carry a machine-checked equivalence witness.

gap: The set-theoretic side is meta-level only: no in-tree formalization of a universe U, of Grothendieck's every-set-in-a-universe axiom, or of the one-universe limitation as a theorem. Also no in-tree witness that the ambient category of sets satisfies the ElementaryTopos axioms at one level: Instance/Sets/Classifier.v proves the classifier for Sets must live one universe up ('its ambient category would have to contain PropSetoid ... one level up'), so Sets is deliberately cross-universe theorems, not an ElementaryTopos instance; the inhabited witness is skeletal FinSet.
